cl_gen_drug_test_times.q: How long do drugs show up on a drug test?
cl_gen_drug_test_times.short: It varies a lot. An expert review says most drugs show in urine for 1.5 to 4 days after one use. In one study, some regular weed smokers were still positive on day 30.
cl_gen_drug_test_times.but: The usual figures come from tiny studies. Some had just one or two people, given one dose in a lab.
how: One expert review sums up: after one use, most drugs showed in urine for 1.5 to 4 days, in blood for 1 to 2 days and in saliva for up to 2 days.

Each figure came from one small study, often measured to a lab's lowest limit. Another chart came from textbooks, older reviews and lab websites. The limit matters: one dose of meth showed for 87 hours at a lab's limit, 43 at a higher cutoff.
Heavy use can last longer than charts say. Among 63 men described as dependent on heroin, 45 in 100 still tested positive for morphine after 6 days. One chart lists 2 days for heroin.

On a locked ward where nobody could smoke, 60 regular weed smokers were tested for up to 30 days. 13 of the 20 with the highest levels were still positive when testing ended. Positives often came back after a negative.
cl_gen_drug_test_times.rate: Mostly second-hand figures from tiny studies, picked by the reviews' authors. The one study that watched people stop counted from arrival, not last use. It stopped watching while many were still positive.

cl_gen_drug_test_false_positives.q: Can medicines cause a false positive on a drug test?
cl_gen_drug_test_false_positives.short: Yes, some can, on certain tests. On one benzo test, 46 of 50 people taking the HIV drug efavirenz screened positive, but a lab check found no benzos.
cl_gen_drug_test_false_positives.but: Most reports describe one or a few people, or a medicine added to urine in a lab. No one has counted how often it happens to people who take them.
how: Quick screens use antibodies, which can grab molecules that look alike. Reviews name sertraline for benzo tests. They name bupropion and pseudoephedrine for amphetamine tests, and some antibiotics for opiate tests.
Only a few numbers exist. In two chart reviews, 41 in 100 unconfirmed amphetamine screens came from people taking bupropion, and about 27 in 100 false benzo screens were linked to sertraline.

Some medicines give true positives, because they are or become the drug tested. Examples: prescribed amphetamines, prescribed THC, and codeine, which turns into morphine. There is no evidence that amoxicillin trips a cocaine test. Numbing drugs like lidocaine do not.
Both reviews say a screen is only a first step. A different lab method should check it before a big decision, like a job or a court case.
cl_gen_drug_test_false_positives.rate: Two expert reviews of single case reports, chart reviews and lab experiments, not studies of how often it happens. Each mix-up was found with certain tests, and some tests have since changed.

general.statement: The detection times on drug-test charts come from big studies.
general.why: Each figure in one review came from one small study, some of just one or two people given one dose. Another chart came from textbooks, older reviews and lab websites.

general.statement: A positive drug screen always means the person took that drug.
general.why: Screens use antibodies that can react to some medicines, like efavirenz on one benzo test. Most reports are single cases. Both reviews say a different lab method should check a screen.

general.statement: Amoxicillin can make a cocaine test positive.
general.why: A clinical review found no evidence behind this popular claim. It says numbing drugs like lidocaine don't trip cocaine tests either.

cannabis.statement: If weed shows up again after a negative test, the person smoked again.
cannabis.why: On a locked ward where nobody could smoke, positives often came back after a negative. That's one study of 60 regular smokers.
